subject: Package for using system fonts in R graphics

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Package for using system fonts in R graphics
parts:
Hi everyone -

I'm working on a package that makes it easy to use use different fonts in PDF output:
  https://github.com/wch/extrafont

Currently it supports only Truetype fonts. This seems to be the most commonly used format on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

It has two external dependencies:
- Ghostscript
- ttf2pt1, a program for extracting/converting afm (font metric) files from ttf files


There are a few things I'd like to do:
1. Remove the dependency on ttf2pt1 by including the source for tt2fpt1 and compiling it on installation.
2. Make sure it works properly on Windows. The only version of Windows that I've tested it on is Windows XP.
3. Add support for Postscript fonts.
4. Make sure it works for Eastern (CJK) fonts.

If you can help with these things -- especially 1 and 2 -- it would be greatly appreciated.


I've attached an example of the output (generated on Ubuntu 12.04) so that you can see that it really works. This is the code used:

setupPdfFonts()

pdf("fonttest.pdf")
qplot(1:5, 1:5) + xlab("Made with extrafont package") + 
  opts(axis.title.x=theme_text(size=14, family="Purisa"))
dev.off()

embedExtraFonts("fonttest.pdf")


-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Package for using system fonts in R graphics
parts:
I've modified the extrafont package to support font packages -- that is R packages that contain font files in a particular directory structure. This should make it easy to distribute fonts on CRAN.

I made a package with the Computer Modern fonts (with symbols) here:
  https://github.com/wch/fontcm/

Installation is straightforward. You'll first need a new version of the extrafont package.

library(devtools)
install_github('extrafont', 'wch')
library(extrafont)

install_github('fontcm', 'wch')
font_install('fontcm')
# When fontcm is on cran, font_install will download from CRAN, install, and 
# register the font with extrafont.

# This will show the registered fonts
fonts()


The fontcm github page shows how to generate the PDF that I've attached. The first page uses R's default fonts, and the second page uses Computer Modern.


One more thing: I've removed extrafont's dependency on the external program ttf2pt1, by including the source code, which gets compiled on install. This means that you need a build environment to install extrafont (until it's on CRAN with precompiled packages).

-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Package for using system fonts in R graphics
parts:
Hm, there might be a drawback to installing the fonts using font packages with extrafont (as opposed to installing the font on the OS, and them importing into extrafont).

If the fonts are installed only via a font package, then people will be able to use the fonts for PDFs and embed them. But then they won't be able to see the fonts for on-screen graphics (which uses fonts from the OS) or for PNG output. For example, when I use CM fonts via the cmfont package, I can only use them in PDFs right now -- they won't show on screen or in a PNG. But maybe (at least for PNG), that's something that can be worked around.

-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Package for using system fonts in R graphics
parts:
For those who are still following along... On the advice of Paul Murrell, I've renamed the package 'fonts', and modified it so that requires a second package, 'fontsdb'. The fontsdb package is basically an empty package that contains the database. 

Previously, when the database was stored in the fonts package, a re-installation or update of fonts would also delete the database. Separating the code and the database into two packages makes it possible to update the code without deleting the database.

Instructions are here: https://github.com/wch/fonts
The only real change is that you need to install fontsdb. Once it's on CRAN, the installation of fontsdb should be automatic.

-Winston
